daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has given BGN one month to fix governance issues in the free meal (MBG) program and instructed all ministries to assist with the overhaul. Coordinating Minister Zulhas is investigating MBG abuses and will report to Prabowo next month. The president has also ordered prioritization of those in need for the program rollout.

  • The Attorney General's Office clarified that former Jampidsus Febrie Adriansyah remains a suspect despite earlier confusion when a new investigation warrant listed him as a witness, following calls by Mahfud and others for KPK to take over the case.
  • President Prabowo will appoint a new Jampidsus this week and has received a nomination letter for Kuntadi, the head of BPA at the Attorney General's Office, to replace Febrie Adriansyah.
  • The Komisi II chairman criticized the work mentality of civil servants, saying they simply clock in, leave for coffee, and clock out again, while a draft ASN law will impose strict KPIs and threaten dismissal for poor performance.
  • PKB reacted to Gus Yahya's statement that Cak Imin was never an NU official and urged NU members to choose a chairman who unifies rather than spreads conflict, as Nasaruddin Umar and Gus Yahya are among candidates for PBNU chairman.
  • The Palace reported to DPR that it successfully reclaimed Hotel Sultan from Pontjo Sutowo through legal proceedings.
  • The government will distribute social aid through village cooperatives Merah Putih, and the Villages Minister announced 20 percent of cooperative profits will become village income.
  • The Home Affairs Minister deferred to West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi on sanctions for Purwakarta's regent, while the DPRD and provincial government agreed on the 2025 budget accountability regulation.
  • The DPR will propose the One Data Indonesia bill as a DPR initiative in an upcoming plenary session.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Four Indonesian Air Force T-50i fighter jets departed for Australia to participate in the Pitch Black 2026 joint military exercise. President Prabowo extended condolences over the death of former Qatari Emir Sheikh Hamad. The DPD chair described China as a strong partner in realizing green democracy for Indonesia.

  • Indonesia's ambassador said that national development visions of Indonesia and China form the foundation for strengthening their partnership.
  • The Palace explained why Prabowo signed a presidential regulation allowing TNI to provide security for prosecutors.

Other

President Prabowo will inaugurate the groundbreaking of the Abadi Masela gas project, a major energy development. Finance Ministry official Purbaya stated that Indonesia's US$443 billion debt remains at a safe level. The government announced that 2025 investment exceeded targets due to downstreaming initiatives.

  • The government assured that B50 biodiesel is safe for engines, though the fuel's rollout requires a national logistics overhaul.
  • Indonesia restarted the TRIGA 2000 reactor to advance nuclear research and has deployed domestically made N219 planes to connect remote regions.
  • The government prioritized family planning for low-income households to reduce stunting, while Papua launched a dashboard to strengthen the free meal program.
  • The Education Ministry said that school gadget restrictions will boost student concentration and urged parents to apply a 3S rule to limit children's gadget use.
  • BPOM complained that MSME assistance missed targets, while Bank Indonesia supports a financial hub to boost external resilience.
